chapter: Probation, Las Vegas and Los Angeles in the 1950s
title: The Melody Room, being hit by a truck and the insurance settlement
summary: After a padlocked club left his bass inside, he was hit by a truck and settled for $1,000.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: What did you do after Las Vegas?
Well, I came back here and Sweets and I went to work with Buddy Rich and Marty Page, at the Melody Room on Sunset Boulevard.

Yeah. And we stayed there quite a while. And then when they left, I stayed on with Benny Carter and Eddie Beall, at the same place. And I went to work one night and they had a padlock on the door. My bass is in there and I had to get the bus home. Benny lived in Hollywood and Eddie Beall lived in Hollywood, so I had to get the bus home. And I got off the bus there at Adams and Western. I was crossing the street and as I got halfway across, here comes a truck down the hill, heading east, his brakes failed, and he hit me and knocked me down. And I just slid off the fender, you know. It didn't hurt me. But I laid there and let them pick me up and take me over to the curb and sit me down, leaning me up against the signal. And I sit there, and I limped over to the truck, got his name and his license number and everything, and he got my address. So the next day they sent an insurance adjuster out to see me. Wanted to know if I was hurt. Well, naturally, I was in my pajamas because musicians sleep late. He thought I was sick, sure enough, in bed. I told him, I said, 'Well, I jammed my fingers, which is my livelihood, when I fell. See, this hand is stiff, this one's swollen. Got a few bruises and got my suit

torn off me." It wasn't torn off me, but oil was ground in it so it wasn't any use. It was a light colored suit, you know, sort of an egg shell color. And they kept sending him around weekly, until I'd hired a lawyer. Now the lawyer said he would get something like 30-percent and I would get 70 percent if it's settled in court. Court battles you can fight forever, you know. And the trucking firm, too, if they had money to fight it with. So finally the adjuster came by and said, "Well, how would you like to settle out of court?" I said, "For how much?" He says, "$800.00". I said, "Oh, no." He said, "Well, how about $1,000.00?" I said, "Well, I'll go along with that, considering my medication and whatnot." I was glad that my instrument wasn't involved, you know. I said, "Otherwise, if I'd been able to get in the club I'd have had my instrument and it would have been broken up." So I bought me a car with the money. Didn't have to ride the bus no more.
Did you ever get your bass back?

Yeah. They had the man that cleans up the club, he had the club open and was cleaning up. For what reason, I don't know. But he was on his job. He had a key. Someone had given him a key to the padlock, so evidently he was cleaning out instead of cleaning up, you know. So after that, I went to Jazz City.
